reasons: Status is 'compliant' and, as expected for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was produced — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals.

The cited text supports the preferred position: § 9.4 limits Customer's exposure on convenience termination to Fees for conforming Services delivered plus a refund of prepaid Fees; § 27.3 confirms force-majeure termination is 'without penalty'; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due. No liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Customer appears in the cited material.

The take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 is correctly identified as the nearest economic analogue but is a minimum-volume obligation properly handled under the dedicated minimum-commitment rule; the playbook's no-double-flag instruction supports not raising it again here, and the rationale flags it transparently rather than hiding it.

Rationale accurately notes that the audit shortfall/true-up amounts are compensatory rather than liquidated damages, so they do not trigger the rule (which applies only when Customer pays an LD or penalty).
